description_en: Nāga Bāhāḥ is one of the largest and well-preserved courtyards in Patan. Thebāhāḥreceived its name from the tradition of painting serpents (nāga) on the walls of twophalcās(LAL4204 and LAL4205). The monastery in the center of the courtyard is known as Paśuvarṇa (or, according to Hemraj Shakya, Vasuvarṇa) Mahāvihāra and houses a statue of Śākyamuni Buddha. The name Yitilañ Vihāra was also recorded during medieval times (Locke1985, 56).The Bāhāḥ is rectangular in shape and connected to other courtyards such as Ilānani, Dhalāyecā, Nyākhācuka, Nāyelakhu, Cheṁko and Jhatapol. It is home to Śākya, Vajrācārya and Dhakwha families. Jośī families live in the adjacent Jośī Nani (courtyard) to the west. Regular worship is performed by Vajrācāryas. The monastery does not have its ownsamghaor esoteric deity (kvāpādhyaḥ).Other statues in the monastery are Mahaṅkāla, Lokeśvara Vasundharā and Tārā. Nāga Bāhāḥ features several important Licchavi sculptures andcaityas alongside more recentcaityas. A shrine known as Nīla Vṛṣiratna (Dvahaḥ Āju) houses an ox that, at irregular intervals (most recently in VS 2062 /2008 CE) is the starting point of a religious pilgrimage (Dīpaṅkara Yātrā). The local community organises ayātrāof circumambulating the Kathmandu Valley (Michaels2013). Nāga Bahāḥ is also the site of the famous Samyak festival. Every four years more than 200 Dipaṅkara Buddhas are brought in a procession to the square where they are worshipped for a day.The current structure of Paśuvarṇa Mahāvihāra dates from around the first quarter of the 20th century but likely rests on much older foundations. The building's design is reminiscent of the "Rana style" that developed in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Originally, the building would probably have been built with regular bricks (ma apa) and decorated with white-washed plaster pilasters on the four corners. In 2007, thevihārawas rebuilt with funding from the Lalitpur Municipality. The removal of deteriorated facade bricks and their replacement with high qualitydaci apabricks was a major change. Most of the original window and door frames were kept, although the shutters and window grilles were re-carved. The roof is covered with the traditionaljhingati(terracotta tiles) laid in a thick bed of mud.
description_ne: क्वाःबहाःबाट (Golden Temple) पश्चिममा यो बहाः अवस्थित छ । क्षेत्रफलको दृष्टिले पाटनमा भएका ठुला बहाःहरूमध्येमा यो पनि पर्दछ । नागबहाः कहलाउने यस बहाःको संस्कृत नाम भने ''पशुवर्ण महाविहार'' हो । हेमराज शाक्यका अनुसार यस बहाःको पूर्वरूप ''पशुवर्ण'' नभई ''वसुवर्ण'' हो ।  मध्यकालीन लिखित स्रोतमा यस बहाःलाई इतिलनेविहार पनि भनिएको छ (Locke1985, 56) ।वर्तमानमा यस बहाःको आफ्नै क्वाःपाःद्य:(kwāḥpāḥ shrine) र संघ नभएकाले Locke(1985, 56)ले यसलाई छुट्टै बहाः (विहार) मानेका छैनन् । बहाः परिसरको केन्द्रमा  पेगोडा शैलीमा निर्मित दुई तले shrine छ जुन २०औं शताब्दीतिर मात्र बनेको हो (Pruscha, 1975 :152 ) ।  shrine भित्र main deity को रूपमा पूर्वाभिमुख Śākyamuni Buddha को मूर्ति छ । Śākyamuni Buddha का अलावा बसुन्धरा, तारा, लोकेश्वरका साथै अन्य स–साना बौद्ध मूर्तिहरू पूर्वतिर फर्काई राखिएको छ (images of Mahāṁkāla, Lokeśvara Basundharā, Tārā and other buddhist icons in the shrine).। यस shrine मा क्वाः बहाः संघका एक बज्राचार्य खलकले विहान नित्य पूजा र बेलुकी तुतः पाठ गर्दै आएका छन् । केन्द्रको shrine अलावा बहाः परिसरमा आकारमा ठुला–साना अनेक शैलीका चैत्यहरू रहेका छन् । बहाःको इशान कोणमा लिच्छविकालीन ढुङ्गेधारा छ  (Lalitpur sub-metropolitan city, 2007 : 30) । उपत्यकाको प्रसिद्ध धार्मिक पर्व दीपंखायात्रासंग सम्बन्धित द्वहःआजुको (नीलवृषरत्न) shrine यसै बहाःको उत्तरमा अवस्थित छ (Michaels2013)। प्रत्यक ४ वर्षमा मनाइने सम्यक पर्व पनि यसै बहाः परिसरभित्र आयोजन हुन्छ ।  दीपंखायात्रा र सम्यक पर्व जस्तो विशेष धार्मिक उत्सवहरू मनाइने बहाः भएकोले  यस बहाःले बेग्लै पहिचान  पाएको छ ।

Pūrṇa Māyā constructed thedharmadhātuin memory of her late husband Pūrṇa Bahādura Nāpit.
Construction of thedharmadhātucaityaby the Lucidyaḥ Guthi from Thyaka Tol.
Restoration of the central shrine building with funds provided by the Lalitpur Sub-Metropolitan City.The restoration was completed on Śrāvaṇa 19, VS 2064.
Restoration of the base of the Nīla Mahāvriṣaratna and addition of a roof by the Shree Nīl Mahā Vriṣa Ratna Boddhisattva Degaḥ Punaḥ Nirmāna Samiti.
Donation of the Ratsambhava statue by the Lucidyaḥ Guthi from Thyaka Tol. The statue was installed anda daśakarma vidhi pūjawas performed.
Thetoraṇabehind the statue of Ratnasambhava was donated by Ratna Kāzi Śākya in memory of his late father Cirī Kāzi Śākya, mother Ratna Māya Śākya, and son Rajendra Śākya.
